segments.say: Lesson 11. Hybrid Search, Reranking & Query Tricks. B M 25 plus dense, R R F, cross-encoder rerankers, multi-query, HyDE and query rewriting.

Plain vector search often misses. Advanced retrieval combines keyword and meaning search, reranks the results with a smarter model, and rewrites vague questions, so the best chunks reach the L L M. Here is an analogy. Hiring: a recruiter quickly skims 500 C Vs (fast search), the manager interviews the top 20 carefully (reranker), and only the best 5 reach the final round (the L L M).

Why does this matter? These are the upgrades interviewers expect you to suggest when "rag isn't accurate enough". A few key words. B M 25: Classic keyword search scoring. Hybrid search: Keyword plus vector search combined. Reranker (cross-encoder): Model that scores query plus chunk together for precise relevance. Query rewriting: L L M rephrases or expands the question before searching. HyDE: Search using a fake generated answer.

segments.say: Hybrid search: run B M 25 (exact keywords) and dense vector search (meaning) in parallel. Each catches what the other misses.

segments.sec: Watch: Two-stage retrieval: recall, then precision
segments.say: Reciprocal Rank Fusion: score equals Σ 1/(k plus rank) across both lists. Merges rankings without calibrating scores. Keep a generous top ~50.

segments.sec: Watch: Two-stage retrieval: recall, then precision
segments.say: Rerank: a cross-encoder reads (query, chunk) together and scores true relevance. Slower, so only run it on the candidates.

segments.sec: Watch: Two-stage retrieval: recall, then precision
segments.say: Send only the best ~5 to the L L M: higher precision, fewer tokens, less distraction. Stage 1 equals recall, stage 2 equals precision.
Query transformations. Users write short, vague or compound questions. Transform the query before retrieving.
Multi-query: generate several paraphrases, retrieve for each and union the results. Better recall for ambiguous wording.
HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings): ask the L L M to draft a plausible answer, then embed that. Answer-shaped text matches answer-shaped chunks better than a short question does.
Decomposition: "Compare our 2024 and 2025 S L A" leads to two retrievals, then combine. Also called sub-question or step-back prompting.

Bi-encoder versus cross-encoder. Bi-encoder (embedding model): encodes query and doc separately, so doc vectors are pre-computed. Fast, scales to millions, less precise. Cross-encoder (reranker): encodes query+doc together, so it sees word-level interactions. Very accurate but can't pre-compute, so you run it on tens of candidates, not millions. Popular rerankers: Cohere Rerank, B G E-reranker, Jina reranker, or an L L M-as-reranker.

Other retrieval upgrades. Metadata filtering & self-query: an L L M extracts filters ("tickets from last week, team=S V S") from the question. Contextual chunk headers: prepend title or section to each chunk before embedding. M M R (Maximal Marginal Relevance): pick relevant and diverse chunks so you don't send 5 near-duplicates. Tune k: retrieve wide (50), rerank, keep narrow (3–8).

Analogy. Hiring: a recruiter skims 500 resumes quickly (bi-encoder / B M 25). The hiring manager deeply interviews the top 20 (cross-encoder). Only the top 5 reach the final round (the L L M context).

Say it in the interview. "I use two-stage retrieval: hybrid B M 25 plus dense with reciprocal rank fusion for recall, then a cross-encoder reranker for precision, sending only the top few chunks. For vague questions I add query rewriting or multi-query, and I validate each addition with recall@k and answer-quality evals, because every stage adds latency and cost.".

Let's compare. Hybrid (B M 25 plus dense): exact terms, I Ds, codes missed by embeddings, +1 index, cheap. Reranker: relevant-but-not-top chunks; noise, +50–300 ms. Query rewriting: typos, follow-ups ("what about it?"), +1 L L M call. Multi-query: ambiguous wording, low recall, N retrievals. HyDE: short queries versus long docs mismatch, +1 L L M call. M M R: duplicate / redundant chunks, cheap.

Bi-encoder versus Cross-encoder. Input: query and doc separately, query plus doc together. Pre-compute docs?: yes, no. Speed: ms over millions, slow, only for tens of docs. Accuracy: good, best. Role: first-stage retrieval, reranking.

A likely interview question: What's reranking and when do you add it? A strong answer: A cross-encoder re-scores retrieved candidates by reading query and chunk together. Add it when the right chunk is retrieved but not ranked high enough, or when context has noise. Budget the extra 50–300 ms.
